question:
A full-term female infant is born by uncomplicated spontaneous vaginal delivery and has Apgar scores
of 8 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes of life, respectively. Her birth weight is 3700 grams. Examination shows
normal respiratory effort, regular heart rate and rhythm without murmur, soft abdomen without masses,
normally formed extremities with acrocyanosis, normal tone, and symmetric Moro reflex. The infant’s
mother is a 19-year-old gravida 1, para 1 woman with well-controlled type 1 diabetes. She has group B,
Rh-positive blood, with negative testing for hepatitis B virus, syphilis, HIV, and group B streptococcus.
She is rubella immune. In addition to glucose levels, which one of the following screening tests is most
likely to be abnormal for this infant in the first few hours of life? Answer Choices: (A) Calcium level (B)
Platelet count (C) Reticulocyte count (D) Hematocrit (E) Blood gas analysis (F) Thyroid function tests
(G) Newborn hearing screen (H) Bilirubin level (I) Serum creatinine level (J) Echocardiography
 A. Hematocrit
B. Blood gas analysis
C. Reticulocyte count
D. Serum creatinine level
E. Thyroid function tests
F. Calcium level
G. Platelet count
H. Newborn hearing screen
I. Bilirubin level
J. Echocardiography
